title: kithctl watch: tail EventSource and fire desktop notifications
description:
Implement kithctl watch: subscribe to kithd EventSource at tailnet IP:port, parse SSE events, call JMAP Message/changes+get for new messages, fire desktop notifications via notify-send/osascript.

WHAT: Bridge kithd state-change events to the desktop user's notification system.

ALGORITHM:
1. Build Config from env + CLI overrides
2. Get tailnet IPs from LocalApiClient::new(&config.ts_socket).status().await?; pick first IP
3. Load TLS cert from config.cert_path() (data_dir/kith.crt): read DER bytes, add as root CA in rustls RootCertStore
4. Build TLS client config with that root store; build TokioTlsConnector
5. Open TCP stream to tailnet_ip:config.port; wrap in TLS via connector.connect(ServerName::try_from("kith.local")?, stream).await?
6. Send HTTP/1.1 GET /jmap/events?types=Message request with headers: Host: kith.local, Accept: text/event-stream, Last-Event-ID: (empty on first connect, then last seen id on reconnect)
7. Read response line-by-line from streaming body; parse SSE frames:
   - Accumulate lines until blank line
   - Extract event type from "event: " prefix
   - Extract data from "data: " prefix; parse as JSON
   - Extract id from "id: " prefix; store as last_event_id
8. On event type "state": deserialize data as {changed: {"a-self": {"Message": "s-N"}}}; if Message key present, proceed to step 9
9. Call JMAP Message/changes: POST /jmap/api with body {"using":["urn:ietf:params:jmap:core","urn:kith:chat:1"],"methodCalls":[["Message/changes",{"accountId":"a-self","sinceState":"{last_message_state}"},"c0"]]}; parse response to get list of created message IDs
10. For each created ID: POST /jmap/api with Message/get; extract sender login and body
11. Truncate body to 80 chars (UTF-8 safe: use char_indices)
12. Fire notification via std::process::Command::new (NOT sh -c):
    - Linux: Command::new("notify-send").arg("Kith").arg(format!("{sender}: {preview}")).status()
    - macOS: Command::new("osascript").args(["-e", &format!("display notification \"{preview}\" with title \"Kith\" with subtitle \"{sender}\"")]).status()
    - Detect platform with cfg!(target_os = ...) at compile time
    - If command fails: log warning, continue (notification failure must not crash watch)
13. On SSE disconnect or IO error: wait 2 seconds, reconnect from step 5 with Last-Event-ID header set
14. Run until SIGINT/SIGTERM (use tokio::signal::ctrl_c().await)

DEFENSIVE RULES:
- NEVER use sh -c for notifications; use Command::new with explicit args
- Truncate body to 80 chars BEFORE passing to notification; use char boundary: let n = body.char_indices().nth(80).map(|(i,_)| i).unwrap_or(body.len()); &body[..n]
- Sanitize sender display name: strip newlines and NUL bytes before using in notification args
- Do not log message body content (PII); only log sender identity and preview length
- Verify TLS cert against pinned cert; fail if cert path does not exist (kithd not yet started)
- on JMAP 403: print "error: not recognized as owner; ensure kithctl runs as the tailnet node owner" and exit(1)
- on JMAP 401: same message
- last_event_id must be a valid "s-N" string or empty string — never pass arbitrary server-supplied value to reconnect header without validation; validate with regex s-\d+

TESTS:
- Unit test: body truncation to 80 chars preserves UTF-8 boundaries (test with emoji/multibyte at boundary)
- Unit test: sender sanitization strips embedded newlines
- Unit test: SSE frame parser correctly parses multi-line frame with event/data/id
- Integration test: deferred to E2E bead (requires live kithd)
